description:

Closes #1063.

title: Add bedrock-mantle support to chat_aws_bedrock()
description:
AWS now serves Bedrock models from two endpoints. The original `bedrock-runtime` endpoint speaks the Converse API, which is what ellmer has always used. The newer `bedrock-mantle` endpoint speaks the Anthropic Messages and OpenAI Responses APIs instead, and hosts models that Converse can't reach at all — including the GPT-5 family, Grok 4.3, and Claude Mythos. Until now those models were simply unavailable through ellmer.

`chat_aws_bedrock()` gains an `api` argument to choose between them. You rarely need to set it: ellmer picks the API from the model name and falls back to Converse for anything it doesn't recognise, so existing code behaves exactly as before.

## Example

```r
# Frontier OpenAI models, which only exist on bedrock-mantle
chat <- chat_aws_bedrock(model = "openai.gpt-5.6-sol")
chat$chat("What is 1 + 1? Just the number.")
#> 2

# Claude through the Anthropic Messages API rather than Converse
chat <- chat_aws_bedrock(model = "anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5", api = "messages")
```

Passing a mantle-only model without an `api` used to fail with a bare "The provided model identifier is invalid". That error now suggests the fix.

## Design decisions

**The argument names the request format, not the endpoint.** `api` takes `"converse"`, `"messages"`, or `"responses"` rather than `"runtime"` and `"mantle"`, because one mantle endpoint serves three different request formats — naming the endpoint wouldn't say which one to send.

**Chat Completions is deliberately not supported.** Every Bedrock model that speaks it also speaks either Converse or Responses, so it would add no model coverage.

**The model lookup is generated, not hand-written.** `data-raw/prices.R` already fetches litellm's model metadata weekly, and that data records which models live only on mantle. It now also writes `R/provider-aws-api.R`, so the table refreshes on the existing schedule. It's a plain R file rather than binary data in `sysdata.rda` so the weekly diff is reviewable.

**The table only lists models Converse can't serve.** Everything else falls through to Converse. This keeps a data refresh from silently moving a working call onto a different endpoint with different quotas — it can only ever turn a failure into a success. It also means an unfamiliar model id (a custom ARN, a new inference profile) keeps working as it does today rather than being rejected.

## Not included

* Bedrock pricing data is missing for all modern Claude ids, so `token_usage()` reports `NA` for them, including on mantle. That's a pre-existing bug in the same extraction script, tracked in #1063.
* Claude Mythos is listed as mantle-only in AWS's docs but doesn't appear in our account's model listing, so those two entries are doc-derived and untested.

## Verification

Live-tested against a real AWS account: basic chat, streaming, tool calling, and structured data all work on `openai.gpt-5.6-sol` via `"responses"`, and on `anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5` via `"messages"`.

That testing caught a bug worth flagging for review: mantle has two OpenAI-compatible paths that are disjoint rather than aliases. Newer models are served from `/openai/v1` and older open-weight ones like gpt-oss from `/v1`, and each rejects the other's models. AWS's API compatibility tables don't record this distinction — only the individual model cards mention it — so the first implementation used `/v1` and failed on exactly the models this PR is meant to unlock.

Note that `test-provider-aws.R:229` currently fails. It's unrelated to this PR — it fails identically on `main`, and was previously invisible because it skips without AWS credentials.

title: Add allow-unsafe-pr-checkout flag
description:
[`actions/checkout@v4.4.0` was released by GitHub on Jul 20, 2026](https://github.com/actions/checkout/releases/tag/v4.4.0), and added an `allow-unsafe-pr-checkout` check defaulting to `false`

The linter workflow now fails with this error

```
Error: Refusing to check out fork pull request code from a 'pull_request_target' workflow. This workflow runs with the base repository's GITHUB_TOKEN, secrets, default-branch cache scope, and runner access. Fetching and executing a fork's code in that trusted context commonly leads to "pwn request" vulnerabilities. To opt in, review the risks at https://gh.io/securely-using-pull_request_target and set 'allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true' on the actions/checkout step.
```

A possible fix is to add `allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true` to the checkout step - this isn't problematic as we're only running the formatter and not the code.

Reported upstream at https://github.com/posit-dev/setup-air/issues/99

title: Add `Round` abstraction over `Turn` history
description:
Closes #507

## Summary

`Chat` stores conversation history as a flat list of `Turn`s
(`system, user, assistant, user(tool-result), assistant, ...`). When tool
calling triggers a loop, several `user`/`assistant` turn pairs accumulate for
what is conceptually a single "round" of interaction. There was previously no
API to get back "the last real exchange" as a unit.

This PR introduces a `Round` S7 class (`R/rounds.R`) that groups the flat
turn list on read, without changing what's stored:

- `Round` has `@input` (the leading input-side turns: any system turns
  followed by the real user turn) and `@response` (a raw list of the
  assistant/tool-result turns that followed), plus a computed `@complete`
  property that reuses the existing `turn_has_tool_request()` predicate from
  the tool loop to determine whether the round finished cleanly.
- `get_rounds(turns)` groups a flat turn list into `Round`s in a single
  linear pass. System turns fold into the `@input` of the round they
  precede rather than appearing as bare elements.
- `Chat$get_rounds(include_system_prompt = FALSE)` and `Chat$last_round()`
  are added as the public API, mirroring `get_turns()`/`last_turn()`.
  `private$.turns` remains the single source of truth; there is
  intentionally no `$set_rounds()`.
- `is_tool_result_turn()` moved from `R/otel.R` to `R/turns.R` so it can be
  shared between `rounds.R` and `otel.R`.
- `format.Round`/`print.Round` follow the existing `Turn` print pattern, and
  a shared `turns_markdown()` helper is used by both `Chat` and `Round`.

A few things worth flagging for review:

- `@response` is a raw list of `Turn`s, not an aggregated result object
  (final text + usage + tool calls). Kept minimal for now since `Chat`
  already has `get_tokens()`/`get_cost()` for cross-turn aggregation; an
  aggregate can be layered on top later without breaking this shape.
- `@complete` treats a round ending in a partial (interrupted/cancelled)
  assistant turn as `FALSE`, not `TRUE` — an in-progress stream isn't a
  finished round.
- `@input` can hold more than one turn: system turns fold into the
  `@input` of the round they precede instead of appearing as bare elements
  in `get_rounds()`'s output, so `@input` is "the input-side turns of the
  round" rather than always a single `UserTurn`. In practice it's almost
  always length-1.
- `Chat$last_round()` always includes system turns (equivalent to
  `get_rounds(include_system_prompt = TRUE)`), even though
  `Chat$get_rounds()` defaults to excluding them, since `last_round()` is
  meant to be a complete historical record.

Full design rationale and alternatives considered (aggregate response object
vs. raw turn list, naming survey against other SDKs) are in the issue
discussion linked above.

## Verification

```r
chat <- chat_openai_test(system_prompt = NULL)
chat$chat("What's 2+2?")
chat$chat("And times 10?")

length(chat$get_rounds())
#> [1] 2

round <- chat$last_round()
round@input      # the last UserTurn
round@response   # list of AssistantTurn(s) for that round
round@complete   # TRUE, since the assistant finished without a pending tool call
```

title: feat(Chat): on_turn_start() callback for mid-loop context compaction
description:
### What
Adds two paired `Chat` callbacks fired inside the tool loop, once per model request (whether or not it involves tools):
- **`on_request_start(turns)`** — fires before each request; receives the complete outgoing request (history + the pending turn) for inspection. Compact mid-loop via `chat$set_turns(compact(chat$get_turns()))`.
- **`on_request_end(turn)`** — fires after each response, before its tool calls run; receives the assistant turn (an `AssistantPartialTurn` if the request was cancelled). Useful for latency/cost tracking.

Both are observation-only (like `on_tool_request`/`on_tool_result`); history is rewritten through the existing public `set_turns()` / `get_turns()`.

### Why
Addresses #1051 — there was no hook firing *inside* the tool loop, once per request, independent of tools (needed for mid-loop context compaction).

### Implementation
Two `CallbackManager`s registered in `initialize()`, invoked at the top of the `while` loop and after `last_turn()` in both `chat_impl` / `chat_impl_async`. Tests cover the `set_turns()` rewrite contract and the async loop; NEWS + docs updated. Supersedes the original single `on_turn_start()` per @gadenbuie's review.

This PR guards the `as_json()` call so it's only made when text is not `NULL`. When it is `NULL`, `compact()` drops the content field from the message, which is the correct shape for a tool-only assistant turn.                                          

Tested locally, and it fixes the failing test.

This PR adds a standardised value "tool_use", so we no longer get those warnings.

title: Expose citation metadata from web search tools
description:
Still a draft as I need to do a proper review of the AI-generated code as there's repetition and ugliness in places.

## Summary

- Adds `Citation` S7 class with `url` and `title` properties, and a `citations` property on `ContentText` and `Turn`
- Extracts citations automatically from Claude, OpenAI, and Google Gemini web search responses
- Fixes streaming for Google grounding metadata (was silently dropped)

## Design decisions

- **Citation is not a Content subclass** -- citations are metadata about text, not standalone content. They don't participate in rendering or get sent back to the model.
- **Only `url` and `title`** -- other provider-specific fields (cited_text, start/end indices) differ in semantics across providers and are omitted. Users can access `turn@json` for raw details.
- **Per-provider extraction helpers rather than a generic** -- the three providers receive citations in completely different shapes and at different levels of the response (Claude: per text block, OpenAI: per text part with mixed annotation types, Google: response-level grounding metadata). A shared generic would need an awkward common interface.
- **Google citations attach to first ContentText** -- since grounding metadata is response-level, not per-part. The single-text-part case is overwhelmingly common.

## Usage

``` r
devtools::load_all("~/ellmer")
#> ℹ Loading ellmer
chat <- chat_claude()
#> Using model = "claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929".
chat$register_tool(claude_tool_web_search())
chat$chat("When was R 4.4.0 released?")
#> R 4.4.0 ("Puppy Cup") was released on the 24th April 2024.
chat$last_turn()@citations
#> [[1]]
#> What’s new in R 4.4.0? | R-bloggers (<https://www.r-bloggers.com/2024/04/whats-new-in-r-4-4-0/>)
```

Closes #775

title: feat: Add tool context and chat store
description:
Closes #871

## Summary

Adds `tool_context()`, a dynamic-scope mechanism that lets tool functions access their calling context during execution — the `ContentToolRequest`, a shared per-conversation store, and conversation history — without polluting the tool's LLM-facing signature.

**Key design decisions:**

- **Dynamic scope over signature injection.** Unlike OpenAI/PydanticAI SDKs that inject context via a magic first parameter, `tool_context()` is opt-in by *calling* — tools that don't need context don't declare anything. This keeps the tool's arguments clean and avoids signature inspection.
- **`chat$store` is a per-conversation environment.** Tools read and mutate it by reference (`ctx$store$n <- ctx$store$n + 1`). It persists across `$chat()` calls and is independently copied by `clone()`.
- **Clone override for store isolation.** R6's `clone()` shares environments by reference, which would silently cross-contaminate stores across clones. Since the person cloning a chat may not be the person who wrote the tools, we override `clone()` (via the [r-lib/R6#178](https://github.com/r-lib/R6/issues/178) workaround) to always deep-clone, eagerly forking the store at clone time. Worth discussing: should we also add a `$fork()` public method as the advertised API for copying a chat, with clone() as the safety net?
- **Async: capture-before-await.** In async tools, `tool_context()` is valid only during the synchronous prefix (before the first `await()`). The tool author captures `ctx <- tool_context()` at the top; since `$store` is an environment, the handle remains live for mutation after awaits.

**New exports:** `tool_context()`, `with_tool_context()`, `local_tool_context()`

## Verification

```r
library(ellmer)

counter_tool <- tool(
  function() {
    ctx <- tool_context()
    ctx$store$n <- (ctx$store$n %||% 0L) + 1L
    paste("Counter is now", ctx$store$n)
  },
  description = "Increment and return the call counter"
)

chat <- chat_openai()
chat$register_tool(counter_tool)
chat$chat("Call the counter three times.")
chat$store$n
#> [1] 3

# Clone gets independent store
chat2 <- chat$clone()
chat2$chat("Call the counter once.")
chat2$store$n
#> [1] 4
chat$store$n
#> [1] 3
```

title: feat: Claude code execution tool and programmatic tool calling
description:
## Summary

This PR adds support for Anthropic's server-side **code execution tool** and **programmatic tool calling (PTC)** to ellmer.

- `claude_tool_code_execution()`: a built-in tool definition that enables Claude's server-side code execution sandbox, including downloading/handling of output files, container reuse across conversation turns, and expired-container recovery.
- `tool(allowed_callers = ...)`: lets a client-defined tool be invoked *programmatically* from inside Claude's code execution environment, not just by the model directly. Tool results are serialized back into the sandbox.

The headline capability is the combination of the two: with programmatic tool calling, data returned by client tools (e.g. a SQL query tool) flows **directly into the code execution sandbox** without passing through the model's context. Without PTC, the model has to regurgitate tool output token-by-token before any code can use it — prohibitively token-inefficient for things like large SQL result sets. With PTC, Claude writes code that calls the tool, receives the result inside the sandbox, and only the final computed answer needs to surface to the model.

Supporting work included here:

- Streaming support for programmatic tool calls, including paused/resumed tool-call turns.
- Prompt-caching breakpoints that remain valid when a conversation ends in a programmatic tool result.
- Conversation state rollback when `chat()`/`stream()` fails mid-tool-loop, so a failed request doesn't corrupt the turn history.
- Replay of server-side tool content on providers that don't support it (OpenAI-compatible, DeepSeek), so a conversation started on Claude can be continued elsewhere without crashing.
- Foundation fix (983f0253): `extra_args$tools` is now appended rather than merged with `utils::modifyList()`, which silently dropped unnamed list entries.

## Minimal example

A local R tool returns an employee's expense rows as JSON. Opting it in via `allowed_callers` lets Claude's *code* call it from inside the sandbox:

```r
library(ellmer)

  expenses <- data.frame(
    employee = c("Emma", "Emma", "Victor", "Tara", "Kai", "Kai"),
    amount = c(2500, 2700, 4100, 1200, 1500, 900),
    category = c("travel", "lodging", "equipment", "software", "software", "office")
  )
  jsonlite::toJSON(
    expenses[expenses$employee == employee, ],
    dataframe = "rows",
    auto_unbox = TRUE
  )
}

  get_expenses,
  description = paste(
    "Look up an employee's expense line items.",
    "Returns a JSON array of objects with fields:",
    "employee (string), amount (number), category (string)."
  ),
  arguments = list(employee = type_string()),
  # Opt in to programmatic tool calling: Claude's *code* may call this tool
  # from inside the code-execution sandbox, not just the model directly.
  allowed_callers = "code_execution_20250825"
)

chat <- chat_anthropic(model = "claude-sonnet-4-6", echo = "all")
chat$register_tool(claude_tool_code_execution())
chat$register_tool(expense_tool)

chat$chat("Which of Emma, Victor, Tara, Kai exceeded their $5000 total expense budget?")
```

## Summary

- `AssistantTurn` gains a `finish_reason` property that standardizes provider-specific stop reasons into a common set: `"success"`, `"max_tokens"`, `"stop_sequence"`, `"content_filter"`, `"context_window"`. Unrecognized reasons are passed through as the raw provider string. `NA_character_` is the default when no provider method exists.
- Finish reason extraction is handled inline in each provider's `value_turn()` method, following the same pattern as `value_tokens()` and `get_token_cost()`.

- OpenAI streaming fix: added `response.incomplete` handler in `stream_merge_chunks` so truncated streaming responses are returned rather than silently dropped as `NULL`.

- **Raw pass-through for unknown values:** Unrecognized stop reasons are returned as-is from the provider rather than mapped to `"other"`, so we have the option to add details to error messages without users needing to dig into `turn@json`.
- **`tool_use` excluded** from the standardized set because ellmer handles tool calls internally -- the user never sees those turns.

title: Add OpenAI Codex Responses subscription provider
description:
## Summary

This PR adds an experimental community-supported provider,
`chat_openai_codex_responses()`, for the ChatGPT Codex Responses backend
at `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`.

The provider is intentionally separate from `chat_openai()`:

- `chat_openai()` uses the OpenAI developer API and `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
- `chat_openai_codex_responses()` uses ChatGPT Codex subscription OAuth
  tokens and the Codex Responses backend.

## User-facing additions

- `chat_openai_codex_responses()` creates an ellmer `Chat` backed by the
  Codex Responses endpoint.
- `openai_codex_credentials()` builds a credentials callback from
  `OPENAI_CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `OPENAI_CODEX_REFRESH_TOKEN`,
  `OPENAI_CODEX_EXPIRES_AT`, and `OPENAI_CODEX_ACCOUNT_ID`.
- `openai_codex_login()` performs a device-code OAuth login flow.
- `openai_codex_refresh()` refreshes an existing Codex OAuth refresh
  token.

## Implementation notes

Reference implementation checked during development: pi’s current OpenAI
Codex OAuth and Responses provider code:

- <https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/ai/src/utils/oauth/openai-codex.ts>

- <https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/ai/src/providers/openai-codex-responses.ts>

- Reuses the existing OpenAI Responses serialization for text, images,
  PDFs, tool calls, tool results, and structured-output schemas.

- Adds Codex-specific request headers:

  - `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
  - `chatgpt-account-id: <account id>`
  - `OpenAI-Beta: responses=experimental`
  - `originator: ellmer`

- Omits `service_tier` when the R argument is `"auto"`, because the
  Codex backend rejects `"auto"` as an explicit service tier value.

- Merges Codex streaming events for function calls
  (`response.output_item.*` and `response.function_call_arguments.*`) so
  ellmer’s existing tool loop can execute local R tools and continue the
  conversation.

- Uses Codex pricing metadata from the pi model table for common Codex
  models, including service-tier multipliers.

## Known limitations / review points

- This provider is experimental and community-supported because it
  targets a ChatGPT subscription backend rather than the public OpenAI
  developer API.
- The Codex backend currently requires streaming responses; the live
  checks below use `$stream()` rather than `$chat(echo = "none")`.
- OAuth `client_id` is a public native-app identifier for the
  Codex-compatible flow, not a user secret. Access tokens, refresh
  tokens, and local credential files must never be committed.

## LLM usage

This provider was added with assistance from the [pi coding
agent](https://pi.dev). The generated and edited code was reviewed, and
the provider behavior was checked with unit tests plus live Codex
Responses runs for text, tool calling, image input, and PDF input.

## Files changed

- `R/provider-openai-codex-responses.R`
- `man/chat_openai_codex_responses.Rd`
- `man/openai_codex_credentials.Rd`
- `tests/testthat/test-provider-openai-codex-responses.R`
- `README.Rmd` / generated `README.md`
- `NEWS.md`
- `DESCRIPTION` / `NAMESPACE`

## Automated checks

Run from the package root:

``` r
pkgload::load_all(".")
testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-provider-openai-codex-responses.R")
```

Expected result at PR prep time: 20 passing expectations.

Also run:

``` sh
R CMD INSTALL --no-docs --no-help --no-html --no-multiarch --with-keep.source .
```

Expected result at PR prep time: install succeeds.

## Live test: text

``` r
chat <- chat_openai_codex_responses(
  model = "gpt-5.5",
  params = params(reasoning_effort = "low"),
  echo = "none"
)

chunks <- coro::collect(chat$stream("Reply with exactly: ellmer codex rmd ok"))
response <- paste0(unlist(chunks), collapse = "")
response
#> [1] "ellmer codex rmd ok\n"

stopifnot(grepl("ellmer codex rmd ok", response, ignore.case = TRUE))
show_tokens(chat)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   input output cached_input cost       input_preview                  cost_exact
#>   <dbl>  <dbl>        <dbl> <ellmr_dl> <chr>                          <chr>     
#> 1    27     22            0 $0.00      Text[Reply with exactly: ellm… $0.000795…
```

## Live test: tool calling

This checks that ellmer can send a tool definition, receive a Codex
function-call stream, execute the local R function, send the tool result
back, and continue the conversation.

``` r
tool_chat <- chat_openai_codex_responses(
  system_prompt = paste(
    "Use tools whenever arithmetic is requested.",
    "After a tool result, give the final answer and do not call tools again."
  ),
  model = "gpt-5.5",
  params = params(reasoning_effort = "low"),
  echo = "none"
)

tool_calls <- 0L

tool_chat$register_tool(tool(
  function(a, b) {
    tool_calls <<- tool_calls + 1L
    a + b
  },
  name = "add_numbers",
  description = "Add two numbers and return their numeric sum.",
  arguments = list(
    a = type_number("The first number."),
    b = type_number("The second number.")
  )
))

tool_chunks <- coro::collect(tool_chat$stream(
  "Use the add_numbers tool to add 6 and 7. Then reply exactly: tool sum is 13"

tool_response <- paste0(unlist(tool_chunks), collapse = "")
tool_response
#> [1] "tool sum is 13\n"

stopifnot(grepl("tool sum is 13", tool_response, ignore.case = TRUE))

vapply(
  tool_chat$get_turns(),
  function(turn) {

#> [1] "ellmer::ContentText"        "ellmer::ContentToolRequest"
```

title: Make use of `finish_reason` and emit warning/error for truncated responses
description:
Closes #3 and closes #867

PR description below is a little long, but there were a lot of weird details I needed to work around, and have included the reasoning for clarity.

## Summary

When a model response is truncated (e.g., because it hit the `max_tokens` limit), ellmer now detects this and surfaces it to the user.

This PR adds a `finish_reason` property to `AssistantTurn` that standardizes provider-specific stop reasons into a common set. A warning is emitted for any truncated response, and `chat_structured()` raises an error before attempting to parse incomplete JSON.

## Code examples

### Before/After for Anthropic

``` r
library(ellmer)

# Claude
chat <- chat_anthropic(
  model = "claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929",
  params = params(max_tokens = 1)
)
chat$chat_structured(
  "Generate a person with a name and age.",
  type = type_object(name = type_string(), age = type_number()),
  echo = "text"
)
#> {"
#> Error:
#> ! parse error: premature EOF
#>                                        {"
#>                      (right here) ------^
chat$chat("Generate a person with a name and age.")
#>
```

and now...

``` r
library(ellmer)

# Claude
chat <- chat_anthropic(
  model = "claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929",
  params = params(max_tokens = 1)
)
chat$chat_structured(
  "Generate a person with a name and age.",
  type = type_object(name = type_string(), age = type_number()),
  echo = "text"
)
#> Warning: Response was truncated because it hit the `max_tokens` limit.
#> {"
#> Error in `extract_data()`:
#> ! Structured data extraction failed because the response was truncated.
#> ℹ The response hit the `max_tokens` limit before the JSON output was complete.
#> ℹ Increase `max_tokens` to allow the model to generate the full response.
chat$chat("Generate a person with a name and age.")
#> Warning: Response was truncated because it hit the `max_tokens` limit.
#> Here
```


## Design decisions

- **Standardized finish reason values:** `"success"`, `"max_tokens"`, `"stop_sequence"`, `"content_filter"`, `"other"`. Each provider maps its API-specific values to this set. `NA_character_` is the default when no provider method exists.

- **`tool_use` excluded** from the standardized set because ellmer handles tool calls internally - the user never sees those turns.

- **`finish_reason` is a public property on `AssistantTurn`**, alongside `tokens`, `cost`, and `duration`. Users can inspect it on any turn.

- **Extraction follows the `value_tokens` pattern:** new S7 generic `value_finish_reason()` with a default method on `Provider` and per-provider overrides for Claude, OpenAI (Responses API), OpenAI-compatible (Chat Completions), Google Gemini, and AWS Bedrock. OpenRouter and Snowflake inherit from OpenAI-compatible.

- **Warning fires early in `TurnAccumulator$value_turn()`**, before the provider parses the response. This ensures the user is told about truncation even if JSON parsing blows up (which happens with OpenAI's eager parsing of structured output).

- **`extract_data()` errors on truncation** before attempting to parse JSON, giving a clear message about increasing `max_tokens`.

- **Both warning and error can fire** for structured chat (warning from `value_turn`, error from `extract_data`). The error is the important one; the warning provides context.

- **OpenAI streaming fix:** added `response.incomplete` handler in `stream_merge_chunks` so truncated streaming responses are returned rather than silently dropped as `NULL`.

title: feat: add `models_list()` S7 generic to Provider class
description:
Closes #986

## Summary

Adds an internal S7 generic `models_list(provider)` that returns a data frame of available models for a given provider. Each provider's `models_*()` standalone function is refactored to delegate to `models_list()`, keeping the public API unchanged.

This lays the groundwork for a future Provider redesign (#499) where `models_list()` could become exported and user-facing. Advanced users and risk-takers can use `ellmer:::models_list()` in the meantime.

**Key design decisions:**

- `models_list()` is internal (non-exported). The base `Provider` method throws a classed `"not_implemented"` error; `ProviderOpenAICompatible` provides a working default for the standard `/models` endpoint.
- A `Chat` dispatch method allows `ellmer:::models_list(chat)` as a convenience.
- Each provider method handles its own URL transformations (e.g., Ollama strips `/v1`, AWS swaps `bedrock-runtime` to `bedrock`) so `models_*()` wrappers stay thin.
- Providers keep their existing return columns -- no standardization across providers.
- A new `ProviderGitHub` class was introduced (empty subclass of `ProviderOpenAICompatible`) so that `chat_github() |> models_list()` correctly dispatches to `/catalog/models` rather than the OpenAI-compatible `/models` default.

**13 methods registered:** base `Provider` (error), `Chat` (delegation), `ProviderOpenAICompatible` (default), plus 10 provider-specific methods for Anthropic, Google (Gemini + Vertex), AWS Bedrock, Ollama, LMStudio, vLLM, DeepSeek, Mistral, GitHub, and Portkey.

title: Add `mcp_connector()` for provider-hosted MCP server connections
description:
Closes #985 (supersedes). ## Summary - Adds `mcp_connector()`, a user-facing API for connecting to remote MCP servers via the provider's API. Both Anthropic and OpenAI are supported. Connectors are registered with `$register_tool()` and the provider handles tool discovery and execution server-side. - Adds `ContentMcpToolRequest`, `ContentMcpToolResult`, and `ContentMcpListTools` content classes that inherit from existing tool content types, so MCP tool calls integrate naturally with conversation display, echo, and streaming. - MCP tool results are echoed during `chat()` and yielded during streaming when `yield_as_content = TRUE`. - Refactors tool result formatting so that echoing tool requests/results during `chat()` and printing a `Chat` object use a consistent display style. Remote MCP servers like DeepWiki can return very large responses (17k+ lines), so tool results are now truncated in both echo output and conversation history, and long tool IDs are shortened for readability. The new formatting arguments flow from high-level methods and are prefixed with `tool_` to avoid collisions. ## Examples ### Anthropic ```r chat <- chat_anthropic() chat$register_tool( mcp_connector("https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp", name = "deepwiki") ) chat$chat("Look up the tidyverse/ellmer repo with your deepwiki tools.") ``` ### OpenAI ```r chat <- chat_openai() chat$register_tool( mcp_connector("https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp", name = "deepwiki") ) chat$chat("Look up the tidyverse/ellmer repo with your deepwiki tools.") ```
Manual configuration without mcp_connector() #### Anthropic ```r chat <- chat_anthropic( model = "claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929", beta_headers = "mcp-client-2025-11-20", api_args = list( mcp_servers = list( list( type = "url", url = "https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp", name = "deepwiki" ) ), tools = list( list( type = "mcp_toolset", mcp_server_name = "deepwiki" ) ) ) ) chat$chat("Look up the tidyverse/ellmer repo with your deepwiki tools.") ``` #### OpenAI ```r chat <- chat_openai( model = "gpt-4.1", api_args = list( tools = list( list( type = "mcp", server_label = "deepwiki", server_url = "https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp", require_approval = "never" ) ) ) ) chat$chat("Look up the tidyverse/ellmer repo with your deepwiki tools.") ```
## Documentation and resources ### Anthropic - [MCP connector docs](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/mcp-connector) — remote MCP server integration guide - Beta header required: `mcp-client-2025-11-20` - Implemented: - MCP server config goes in a separate `mcp_servers` body field; tools use `type: "mcp_toolset"` - Tool calls appear as separate `mcp_tool_use` and `mcp_tool_result` content blocks - Result content blocks can contain `text`, `image`, and `document` types - Auth via `authorization_token` field on the server config entry - Not implemented: - **Tool filtering on `mcp_toolset`**: `default_config` object with `enabled` and `defer_loading` booleans applied to all tools; `configs` named object with per-tool overrides keyed by tool name, each with its own `enabled`/`defer_loading`. Together these enable allow-listing (disable all by default, enable specific tools) or deny-listing individual tools. - **`cache_control` on `mcp_toolset`**: Prompt caching breakpoint on the toolset entry itself, similar to `cache_control` on other tool types. ### OpenAI - [Remote MCP servers guide](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/tools-remote-mcp-servers) — MCP tool connector docs - No beta header needed (production API) - Implemented: - MCP config is inline as a `type: "mcp"` tool entry - Tool calls appear as merged `mcp_call` output blocks (request + result combined); tool discovery uses `mcp_list_tools` output blocks - `require_approval` support (`"never"` by default in ellmer); `mcp_approval_request` triggers an informative error - Auth via `authorization` field on the tool entry - Not implemented: - **Built-in OAuth connectors**: Pre-built connectors identified by `connector_id` (e.g. `connector_gmail`, `connector_google_drive`, `connector_dropbox`) that use OAuth tokens instead of an arbitrary server URL. Our `mcp_connector()` only supports `server_url`. - **Granular `require_approval`**: Object form allowing per-tool approval control, e.g. `{never: {tool_names: ["tool_a", "tool_b"]}}`, so specific tools can bypass approval while others require it. - **Interactive approval workflow**: When `require_approval` is not `"never"`, the API returns an `mcp_approval_request` output and expects an `mcp_approval_response` input in a follow-up request. We currently error instead of surfacing the approval request to the user.

title: Introduce ContentThinkingDelta for streaming thinking
description:
## Summary

Addresses #974 by introducing a `ContentThinkingDelta` class that cleanly separates streaming thinking fragments from complete `ContentThinking` objects stored in turn history.

- **`stream = "text"`**: Thinking is suppressed from yielded chunks entirely (consumers only see response text)
- **`stream = "content"`**: Thinking fragments are yielded as typed `ContentThinkingDelta` objects with a `phase` property (`"start"`, `"body"`, or `"end"`) that communicates block boundaries
- **Console echo**: Thinking is always echoed wrapped in `<thinking>` / `</thinking>` tags so users can distinguish it from response text



## Examples

### `$chat()` — thinking echoed with tags

```r
chat <- chat_anthropic(
  model = "claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
  params = params(budget_tokens = 1024, max_tokens = 2048)
)

chat$chat("What is 2+2? Think carefully.")
```

Console output:

```
<thinking>
This is a very basic arithmetic question. 2 + 2 = 4. The human is asking me to
"think carefully" but this is straightforward addition. There's no trick here -
it's just basic math.
</thinking>

2 + 2 = 4

This is a fundamental addition problem. When you add 2 and 2 together, you get
4.
```

### `$stream(stream = "text")` — thinking suppressed from yielded chunks

```r
chat <- chat_anthropic(
  model = "claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
  params = params(budget_tokens = 1024, max_tokens = 2048)
)

chunks <- coro::collect(chat$stream("What is 2+2? Think carefully.", stream = "text"))
cat(paste0(chunks, collapse = ""))
```

Output:

```
2 + 2 = 4

I thought carefully about this, and it's straightforward addition. Two plus two
equals four.
```

## Design decisions

- **Two classes**: `ContentThinking` (complete thought, stored in turns, `format()` wraps in tags) vs `ContentThinkingDelta` (streaming fragment, never stored in turns, `format()` returns bare text)
- **Providers emit `ContentThinkingDelta`**: Providers stay simple — they just emit deltas with the default `phase = "body"`. The central streaming layer annotates phase based on transitions.
- **Sentinel end marker**: The `phase = "end"` delta has empty thinking text and signals "thinking has ended" without requiring look-ahead buffering.
- **No tag injection into the stream**: Typed objects carry boundary information — consumers decide how to render. This addresses @gadenbuie's feedback that objects should carry structure, not strings.


## What downstream consumers (shinychat) get

```
ContentThinkingDelta("first reasoning...", phase = "start")
ContentThinkingDelta("more reasoning...", phase = "body")
ContentThinkingDelta("", phase = "end")
ContentText("Here is my response...")
```

Shinychat can:
1. Route thinking deltas to the thinking panel with `content_type: "thinking"` wire flag
2. Use `phase` to manage stored-message boundaries (prepend `<thinking>\n` on start, append `\n</thinking>\n\n` on end)
3. Keep its existing client-side tag parser for raw-tag models (DeepSeek, QwQ)

## Test plan

- [x] `stream = "text"` suppresses thinking from yielded output
- [x] `stream = "content"` yields `ContentThinkingDelta` objects with correct phase sequence (start → body → end)
- [x] Thinking chunks precede text chunks in stream order
- [x] All existing tests pass

title: Fix tool calling in Snowflake provider
description:
The PR fixes tool calling in `chat_snowflake()`, which is currently completely broken. Any use of tools (including via querychat) errors with:

```
Error in `if (content$type == "text") ...`:
! argument is of length zero
```

**Reprex** (fails on main, passes on this branch):

```r
library(ellmer)

chat <- chat_snowflake(
  system_prompt = "Always use your tools when asked.",
  account = Sys.getenv("SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT")
)
chat$register_tool(tool(
  function(x) paste("result:", x * 2),
  name = "double_number",
  description = "Doubles a number",
  arguments = list(x = type_number("The number to double"))
))

chat$chat("Double the number 5")
```

**Root cause:** Snowflake's streaming API can send `tool_use` as the very first chunk (with no preceding text). The old `stream_merge_chunks` assumed responses always started with text. When they didn't, `content_list` entries ended up without a `type` field, which crashed `value_turn()`.

We didn't catch this because `test_tools_simple(chat_snowflake)` requires live credentials and is always skipped in CI (via `default_snowflake_credentials()` → `testthat::skip()` at `R/provider-snowflake.R:470`).

**Fixes (each a separate commit for clarity):**

1. **Fix `stream_merge_chunks`** — Handle tool_use-first responses; use positional search instead of hardcoded indices; normalize `content_list` entries with explicit `type` fields.
2. **Add `stream_content` override** — Snowflake uses `delta$text`, not `delta$content`. Without this, `stream = "content"` mode (used by querychat) never yielded text during streaming.
3. **Handle tool-only turns in `as_json`** — Once tools parse correctly, the follow-up request failed because serializing a `ContentToolRequest`-first turn was unhandled.
4. **Filter empty text in `value_turn`** — Snowflake sends a final empty text delta; if included in the Turn and sent back as history, the API rejects it with "text content blocks must be non-empty".

Closes #938

## Test plan

- [x] Existing offline chunk-merge test updated for new format
- [x] New offline test for tool_use-first chunk merging (the #938 scenario)
- [x] New offline test for `stream_content` extraction from Snowflake's delta format
- [x] New offline test for `as_json` with tool-only assistant turns
- [x] Verified end-to-end against live Snowflake API (non-streaming + streaming + content mode)

title: Add ContentThinking support to OpenAI-compatible providers
description:
## Summary

- Extract `reasoning_content` from streaming deltas and non-streaming responses in `ProviderOpenAICompatible`, producing `ContentThinking` objects in the assistant turn.
- Add a `preserve_thinking` parameter (default `FALSE`) that controls whether reasoning content is sent back to the API in multi-turn conversations. When `FALSE`, thinking is captured in the turn but filtered from subsequent requests.
- Set `preserve_thinking = TRUE` for OpenRouter, which recommends including reasoning traces in conversation history.

## Motivation

Providers disagree on whether reasoning traces should be included in multi-turn conversation history:

| Provider | Requirement |
|----------|------------|
| DeepSeek | **Must exclude** — returns 400 if `reasoning_content` is included in input messages |
| Fireworks AI | **Must include** — required for multi-turn tool-calling with thinking models |
| OpenRouter | **Should include** — recommended for quality, especially with tool-calling |
| Groq | Not documented |
| Together AI | Not documented |
| Azure, Cloudflare, Databricks, Portkey, Snowflake | Don't return `reasoning_content` in chat completions (N/A) |

The `preserve_thinking` parameter (default `FALSE`) lets each provider wrapper choose the correct behavior. The default matches DeepSeek's requirement since it's the most common reasoning model accessed via OpenAI-compatible APIs.

## Verification

```r
library(ellmer)

# With a reasoning model via OpenRouter
chat <- chat_openrouter(model = "deepseek/deepseek-r1")
chat$chat("What is 2+2? Think step by step.")
# ContentThinking appears in the turn
chat$last_turn()@contents
```

title: Lazy price cache with automatic refresh from GitHub
description:
Builds on #967 which handles the GHA/data-raw infrastructure.

## Summary

Adds a user-controlled caching layer (`R/prices.R`) that keeps model pricing data fresh without requiring a package update. Users call `models_update_prices()` to download and cache the latest `prices.json` from GitHub; `prices()` then merges cached rows with the packaged data, with cached rows winning on conflicts.

- Cached prices are stored as RDS in `tools::R_user_dir("ellmer", "cache")`
- Uses HTTP ETag to skip downloads when data hasn't changed
- `prices.json` is now a versioned envelope (`schema_version`, `min_ellmer_version`, `data`); incompatible cached files are detected and discarded rather than silently merged
- Informs the user with a clickable link when pricing data is actually updated

## Key design decisions

- **`models_update_prices()` is user-initiated**: There is no automatic background refresh. Users call `models_update_prices()` when they want to pull the latest pricing data; ellmer's bundled snapshot covers the common case between updates.
- **ETag-based caching**: Each call to `models_update_prices()` makes at most one cheap 304 request if the upstream data hasn't changed since the last successful download.
- **Cached rows win on key conflicts**: When merging cached and bundled prices, cached rows take precedence so that updated prices override stale bundled data.
- **Schema versioning guards cache compatibility**: `prices.json` carries a `schema_version` integer. `prices()` rejects cached data whose version differs from the bundled data and falls back gracefully with an informative message. `prices_cache_download()` rejects remote data whose version differs from the bundled data with a clear error.
- **Informative errors on download failure**: Network errors, unexpected HTTP status codes, malformed JSON, and schema mismatches all surface as actionable `cli::cli_abort()` messages rather than silent failures.
- **Eager cache population after update**: `models_update_prices()` calls `prices()` immediately after clearing `the$prices` so the new data is loaded into the session cache before returning.

## Test plan

- [x] `prices()` merge logic: cached wins on key conflict, falls back to bundled when no cache
- [x] `prices()` schema version: informs and falls back to bundled when cached version is older; warns and falls back when cached version is newer
- [x] `models_update_prices()`: informs and returns TRUE when download succeeds (cache pre-populated); informs and returns FALSE when already up to date
- [x] `prices_cache_download()` at the curl boundary: 200 writes cache with schema_version and ETag; 304 returns FALSE; HTTP error aborts; curl error aborts; malformed JSON aborts; missing envelope fields abort; remote schema newer than bundled aborts with upgrade message; remote schema older than bundled aborts; missing required columns abort; non-numeric input/output abort

title: feat(aws): Support reasoning/thinking content for extended thinking
description:
Fixes #964

## Summary

Adds support for `reasoningContent` blocks in the AWS Bedrock provider, enabling extended thinking in Anthropic Claude models hosted on Bedrock.

- **Streaming:** `stream_merge_chunks()` now handles `reasoningContent` deltas (both `text` and `signature` sub-fields), accumulating them alongside text and tool-use blocks.
- **Turn parsing:** `value_turn()` converts `reasoningContent` blocks in Bedrock responses into `ContentThinking` objects, making thinking content accessible on `chat$last_turn()@contents`.
- **Round-trip serialization:** A new `as_json(ProviderAWSBedrock, ContentThinking)` method serializes `ContentThinking` back to the `reasoningContent` wire format (including the opaque `signature` field required by Bedrock for multi-turn conversations).
- **Documentation:** Updates `?chat_aws_bedrock` `api_args` example to show how to enable thinking via `additionalModelRequestFields`.

## Verification

Enable extended thinking by passing `additionalModelRequestFields` in `api_args`:

```r
chat <- chat_aws_bedrock(
  params = params(temperature = 1),
  api_args = list(
    additionalModelRequestFields = list(
      thinking = list(type = "enabled", budget_tokens = 4000)
    )
  ),
  model = "us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0"
)
```

Unfortunately, I think the shape of `additionalModelRequestFields` is going depend on the specific model being used, which is why I did not try to wire this up through `params()`.

```r
# Streaming
chat$chat("Create a riddle for data scientists")
chat
#> <Chat AWS/Bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0 turns=2 input=43 output=520>
#> ── user ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Create a riddle for data scientists
#> ── assistant [input=43 output=520] ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> <thinking>
#> Let me create a riddle that would appeal to data scientists...
#> </thinking>
#>
#> I live in forests but have no roots...

# Conversation can be continued
chat$chat("that was funny!")

# Non-streaming
chat$set_turns(list())
chat$chat("Create a riddle for data scientists", echo = "none")
```

Adds `chat_lmstudio()` and `models_lmstudio()` as a new provider for [LM Studio](https://lmstudio.ai), a local model server available on Mac, Windows, and Linux with an OpenAI-compatible API. LM Studio is particularly notable for its excellent support for Apple's MLX inference engine, making it a compelling choice for local inference on Apple Silicon.

The implementation follows `chat_ollama()` as a template — both are local OpenAI-compatible servers — with key differences: default port `1234`, `LMSTUDIO_BASE_URL` env var, and model management via the LM Studio GUI rather than a CLI pull command.

`ProviderLMStudio` extends `ProviderOpenAICompatible` and requires no custom `as_json` overrides (tool calling works with inherited OpenAI defaults). `chat_params` is overridden to map `frequency_penalty`, `presence_penalty`, `seed`, `stop`, `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, and `max_tokens`. `has_lmstudio()` checks connectivity before making requests, and `models_lmstudio()` queries the standard `/v1/models` endpoint. Test helpers auto-discover the first loaded model (preferring `google/gemma-4-26b-a4b` or `zai-org/glm-4.7-flash`), since LM Studio models are GUI-managed.

## Summary

- Adds a `cache` parameter to `chat_aws_bedrock()` with options `"auto"` (default), `"5m"`, `"1h"`, and `"none"`.
- `"auto"` enables 5-minute caching for models known to support it (Anthropic Claude and Amazon Nova) and disables caching for all other models. This avoids HTTP 403 errors from Bedrock when `CachePointBlock` is sent to unsupported models.
- Inserts `CachePointBlock` entries in the system prompt and last message turn of each request via `bedrock_cache_point()` helper.
- Reports `cacheReadInputTokens` from the Bedrock Converse API response in token usage tracking.

title: feat: Cancel streaming responses
description:
Fixes #643

## Summary

Adds graceful handling when a stream ends early — whether by programmatic cancellation, user interrupt, or error — so that partial responses are preserved in chat history.

1.  **`stream_controller()`** — a cooperative cancellation handle for programmatic use (e.g. Shiny “Cancel” buttons), with `$cancel()` and `$reset()` methods. Controllers can be reused across streams; passing a pre-cancelled controller warns and auto-resets.
2.  **`AssistantPartialTurn`** — a new S7 class (inherits `AssistantTurn`) that marks incomplete turns in history, with appropriate print formatting.
3.  **Incremental turn saving** — streaming turns are written to chat history as chunks arrive, not after the stream completes. The partial `AssistantPartialTurn` survives any form of interruption and is either replaced with a complete `AssistantTurn` when the API finishes a streaming turn, or remains an `AssistantPartialTurn` if the streaming is interrupted by an early exit (error, interrupt, cancel).

This biggest change of this PR is that now, after any early exit, the conversation history will contain the partial response. This allows the user to continue the conversation from where it was interrupted.

## Motivation

Today, `$stream()` and `$stream_async()` hand back coro generators that yield chunks until the model finishes. The only way to stop early is to break out of the `for` / `coro::loop` body — which works when you control the loop, but doesn’t work when the generator is consumed by third-party code (e.g. `shinychat::markdown_stream()`). There’s no handle to reach in and say “stop after the current chunk.”

Similarly, pressing Ctrl-C during a streaming `$chat()` would lose the partial response entirely — no turns were added to history, so the conversation had no record of the exchange, even though in many cases the user would have seen the model’s response.

## How it works

### The controller object

`stream_controller()` returns a lightweight environment with class `ellmer_stream_controller`:

``` r
ctrl <- stream_controller()
ctrl$cancelled   # FALSE
ctrl$cancel()    # flips cancelled to TRUE
ctrl$reset()     # flips cancelled back to FALSE
```

Controllers can be reused across streams. Passing a pre-cancelled controller to `$stream()` or `$stream_async()` issues a warning and auto-resets it, preventing silent empty partial turns from stale references.

This emulates patterns from JavaScript where an `AbortController` is used to close a fetch request

``` js
const controller = new AbortController();
const response = await fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal, ... });
// To cancel:
controller.abort(); // throws AbortError, closes TCP connection
```

### Plumbing through the call stack

The `controller` argument is threaded from the public API all the way down to the httr2 perform layer:

    $stream(controller=)
      → Chat$._stream_turn_complete()
        → Chat$.submit_turns()
          → chat_perform(controller=)
            → chat_perform_stream(controller=)   # coro::generator

(Same path for `$stream_async()` → `chat_perform_async_stream()`.)

### Cancellation check point

Inside both `chat_perform_stream` and `chat_perform_async_stream`, the `controller$cancelled` flag is checked at the top of the `repeat` loop, before calling `chat_resp_stream()`:

``` r
repeat {
  if (!is.null(controller) && controller$cancelled) {
    break
  }
  event <- chat_resp_stream(provider, resp)
  # ...
}
```

When cancelled, the generator breaks out of the loop. Because `resp_perform_connection()` is protected by `on.exit(close(resp))`, the underlying HTTP connection is always cleaned up — whether the stream completes naturally, is cancelled, or errors.

The check happens *before* the next `chat_resp_stream()` call, so cancellation takes effect between chunks rather than mid-read. This avoids any concern about interrupting httr2’s connection-level read.

### Incremental turn saving with `AssistantPartialTurn`

Previously, turns were added to `private$.turns` only after the streaming loop completed. Any interruption — Ctrl-C, error, or the user simply abandoning a `$stream()` generator — meant the partial response was lost.

Now `submit_turns()` uses an **optimistic write** pattern with a dedicated partial turn class:

1.  **Before the first chunk:** eagerly call `add_turn(user_turn, AssistantPartialTurn(), log_tokens = FALSE)` to place both turns in history. The `AssistantPartialTurn` class (inherits `AssistantTurn`) marks the turn as incomplete.
2.  **On each chunk:** `update_turn_contents(private, turn_idx, content)` appends the new `Content` object to the partial turn in place
3.  **On normal completion:** replace the `AssistantPartialTurn` with the full `AssistantTurn` from `value_turn()` (which has tokens, cost, tool calls) and log tokens
4.  **On any early exit:** `on.exit(finalize_partial_turn(...))` fires automatically, merging adjacent `ContentText` fragments. The turn stays as an `AssistantPartialTurn` in history.

Because the turn is in history from the very first chunk, it survives interrupts at *any* point: inside the streaming loop, between generator yields, during tool invocation, or in user code consuming `$stream()` chunks.

The tool-calling loop in `chat_impl` also breaks early when `controller$cancelled` is set — a partial turn shouldn’t trigger tool execution.

### Cleanup via `on.exit()`

Turn finalization uses `on.exit()` rather than `tryCatch` error/interrupt handlers. This means errors and interrupts propagate naturally through the call stack — no catching and re-throwing. The `finalize_partial_turn()` function checks the turn class: it’s a no-op for complete `AssistantTurn` objects (normal completion replaces the partial with a full turn before `on.exit` fires), and only merges `ContentText` fragments for `AssistantPartialTurn`.

### Print formatting

`AssistantPartialTurn` shows `[interrupted]` in the Chat print output instead of `[input=NA output=NA]`:

    ── assistant [interrupted] ──────────────────────
    The beginning of the response before it was cut off...

Token accounting (`get_tokens()`, `get_cost()`, and the Chat header) excludes partial turns so that `NA` values don’t propagate into totals. This is documented in the `get_cost()` help page.

## Examples

### Sync — cancel after N chunks

``` r
pkgload::load_all()
chat <- chat_openai(model = "gpt-5.4-mini")

ctrl <- stream_controller()
stream <- chat$stream("Write a story.", controller = ctrl)

i <- 0
coro::loop(for (chunk in stream) {
  i <- i + 1
  cat(chunk)
  if (i > 10) ctrl$cancel()
})
```

### Async — cancel after N seconds

``` r
ctrl2 <- stream_controller()
chat2 <- chat_claude()
stream2 <- chat2$stream_async(
  "Write a short story.",
  controller = ctrl2
)

cat("Class:", paste(class(stream2), collapse = ", "), "\n\n")

# Cancel after 5s
later::later(
  function() {
    cat("\n[cancelling async stream]\n\n")
    ctrl2$cancel()
  },
  delay = 5
)

p <- coro::async(function() {
  for (chunk in coro::await_each(stream2)) {
    cat(chunk)
  }
})()

sync(p)
```

### Async in Shiny — cancel on button click

``` r
controller <- stream_controller()

chat_task <- ExtendedTask$new(function(user_query, controller = NULL) {
  chat <- chat_openai(model = "gpt-4.1-nano")

  # Stream the chat completion into the markdown stream.
  stream <- chat$stream_async(user_query, controller = controller)
  shinychat::markdown_stream("response", stream)
})

observeEvent(input$ask, {
  controller <<- stream_controller()
  chat_task$invoke(input$query, controller = controller)
})

observeEvent(input$cancel, {
  controller$cancel()
})
```

<details><summary>Full app example</summary>

``` r
library(shiny)
library(bslib)
pkgload::load_all()
library(ellmer)
library(promises)
library(shinychat)

ui <- page_sidebar(
  title = "Interactive chat with async",
  sidebar = sidebar(
    textAreaInput("user_query", "Tell me a story about...", "unicorns"),
    input_task_button("ask_chat", label = "Generate a story"),
    actionButton("cancel_chat", "Cancel generation", disabled = TRUE)
  ),
  card(
    card_header("Your Story"),
    shinychat::output_markdown_stream("response"),
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  chat_task <- ExtendedTask$new(function(user_query, controller = NULL) {
    # We're using an Extended Task for chat completions to avoid blocking the
    # app. We also start the chat fresh each time, because the UI is not a
    # multi-turn conversation.
    chat <- chat_openai(
      system_prompt = "You are a rambling chatbot who likes to tell stories but gets distracted easily.",
      model = "gpt-4.1-nano"
    )

    # Stream the chat completion into the markdown stream.
    stream <- chat$stream_async(user_query, controller = controller)
    shinychat::markdown_stream("response", stream)
  })

  bind_task_button(chat_task, "ask_chat")

  controller <- stream_controller()

  observeEvent(input$ask_chat, {
    updateActionButton(session, "cancel_chat", disabled = FALSE)
    chat_task$invoke(input$user_query, controller = controller)
  })

  observeEvent(input$cancel_chat, {
    controller$cancel()
    updateActionButton(session, "cancel_chat", disabled = TRUE)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

</details>

title: Extend ToolBuiltIn with description and annotations
description:
Closes #942

## Summary

Extends the `ToolBuiltIn` S7 class with `description` and `annotations` properties, making the metadata available to downstream consumers like shinychat.

Rather than having `ToolBuiltIn` extend `ToolDef`, we added only the relevant properties directly to `ToolBuiltIn`. This is intentional: `ToolDef` wraps an R function — it exists to let users define tools as R code. Built-in tools like `openai_tool_web_search()` are provider-native capabilities with no corresponding R function, so inheritance from `ToolDef` would be semantically wrong. Instead, `ToolBuiltIn` now carries the `description` and `annotations` fields that downstream packages need.

All provider-specific built-in tool constructors (`openai_tool_web_search()`, `claude_tool_web_search()`, `claude_tool_web_fetch()`, `google_tool_web_search()`, `google_tool_web_fetch()`) are updated to populate these fields using `tool_annotations()` with `read_only_hint = TRUE` and `open_world_hint = TRUE`, accurately reflecting that these tools read from the web without modifying state.

## Verification

Built-in tools now expose metadata the same way user-defined tools do:

```r
tool_web <- claude_tool_web_search()
tool_web@description
#> [1] "Search the web for up-to-date information."
tool_web@annotations
#> $title
#> [1] "Web search"
#> $read_only_hint
#> [1] TRUE
#> $open_world_hint
#> [1] TRUE
```

title: Fix streaming web search results
description:
Closes #941

## Summary

Three bugs caused errors when streaming web search results:

1. **Claude `citations_delta` at wrong nesting level** — The handler was dead code at the top level of `stream_merge_chunks()`, but `citations_delta` events arrive inside `content_block_delta` chunks. They fell through to the "Unknown delta type" warning. Moved the handler into the correct branch.

2. **Claude `server_tool_use` input not parsed from JSON** — During streaming, `stream_merge_chunks()` accumulates `content$input` as a raw JSON string. `value_turn()` already parsed this for `tool_use` but not for `server_tool_use`, causing `"$ operator is invalid for atomic vectors"`. Added the same `is_string()` / `parse_json()` guard.

3. **OpenAI `web_search_call` with non-search action types** — Newer models return `open_page` and `find_in_page` actions that lack a `query` field. Added a fallback chain (`query` → `queries[[1]]` → `url` → `"web search"`) with a length guard for empty `queries` lists.

Also fixed a pre-existing partial argument match warning (`url` vs `urls` in `ContentToolResponseSearch()`).

## Verification

```r
library(ellmer)

# Claude streaming web search
chat <- chat_anthropic(
  model = "claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
  tools = list(tool_web_search())
)
chat$chat("What's the latest R release?")

# OpenAI streaming web search
chat <- chat_openai(
  model = "gpt-4.1-mini",
  tools = list(tool_web_search())
)
chat$chat("What's the latest R release?")
```

title: Fix gargle credentials skipped in interactive mode
description:
Closes #922.

In `default_google_credentials()`, the `is_interactive()` check on line 733 unconditionally returned the OAuth browser flow, even when `gargle::token_fetch()` had already obtained a valid token from application default credentials (e.g. via `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`). This meant that in interactive sessions (RStudio, Shiny), service account credentials were silently ignored.

The fix adds an `is.null(token)` guard so the OAuth fallback only activates when no token was obtained via gargle. This matches the [documented authentication order](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org/reference/chat_google_gemini.html#authentication) and is consistent with how the Azure and Databricks providers handle their interactive OAuth fallbacks.

description:
## Summary

Adds batch processing support for `chat_groq()` via the Groq Batch API (50% cost discount, 24h completion window). Closes #914 (Groq portion — Gemini batch was #926).

Implements six batch methods on `ProviderGroq` (`has_batch_support`, `batch_submit`, `batch_poll`, `batch_status`, `batch_retrieve`, `batch_result_turn`), reusing OpenAI's `openai_upload`, `openai_download_file`, and `openai_json_fallback` helpers (the bodies are identical).

## Implementation notes

- Mirrors the existing OpenAI batch JSONL format (`custom_id` / `method` / `url` / `body`) but targets Groq's `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint.
- `batch_status` maps Groq's terminal states (`completed`, `failed`, `expired`, `cancelled`) to `working = FALSE` — OpenAI's bare `!= "completed"` check would busy-poll forever on a failed/expired Groq batch.
- `batch_retrieve` guards `output_file_id` / `error_file_id` with `length() == 1 && nzchar()` because Groq returns `"error_file_id": {}` (empty JSON object) for successful batches.
- `batch_result_turn` uses Gemini's safer guard (`!is.null(result) && result$status_code == 200L && !is.null(result$body)`) so failed/expired rows from the error file don't crash.

## Tests

Two fixture-based tests in `tests/testthat/test-provider-groq.R`:
- `batch chat works` — text path, `llama-3.1-8b-instant`
- `batch_chat_structured works` — structured path, `openai/gpt-oss-20b`

Fixtures (`tests/testthat/batch/state-capitals-groq.json`, `state-capitals-groq-structured.json`) were recorded against live Groq.

title: Handle invalid JSON in GitHub Models 429 responses
description:
Closes #901

## Description
This PR fixes a crash in `chat_github` (and other OpenAI-compatible providers) when the API returns a 429 rate limit error with a text body but a `Content-Type: application/json` header.

Previously, `ellmer` would crash with a JSON parsing error (`lexical error: invalid char in json text`) before `httr2` could detect the 429 status and trigger a retry.

title: fix: Tool content previews and expanded turns
description:
Two fixes for content items in tool results:

1. Adds `tool_string_preview()` that actively avoids failing to prevent tool call displays from breaking the chat flow. My take is that tool displays are incidental; only API failures should be catastrophic.

2. When a turn contains multiple tool results that need to be expanded, we need to ensure that the tool results are ordered first in the reply message, rather than interleaved with other content.

``` r
pkgload::load_all()
#> ℹ Loading ellmer

get_cat_image <- function() {
  size <- sample(200:300, 1)
  url <- sprintf("https://placecats.com/%d/%d", size, size)

  tmpf <- withr::local_tempfile(fileext = ".jpg")
  download.file(url, tmpf, quiet = TRUE)

  content_image_file(tmpf, resize = "none")
}

chat <- chat("anthropic/claude-3-5-haiku-20241022", echo = "output")
chat$register_tool(
  tool(
    function(n_images = 1) {
      if (n_images == 1) {
        get_cat_image()
      } else {
        res <- vector("list", n_images * 2)
        for (i in seq_len(n_images)) {
          res[[i * 2 - 1]] <- ContentText(paste0("Cat image ", i, ":"))
          res[[i * 2]] <- get_cat_image()
        }
        res
      }
    },
    name = "get_cat_image",
    description = "Gets a random cat image.",
    arguments = list(
      n_images = type_integer("Number of cat images to get at once.")
    )
  )
)
```

On `main`, the next lines work if you have `echo = "none"`, as in the API calls work as expected, but printing the tool result (`echo = "output"`) fails. This PR replaces an error with a message that the tool result can't be displayed. If we can't serialize the tool result to send in the API payload, we'll get an error at that step instead.

```r
chat$chat(
  "Get 2 random cat images and describe what the cats are feeling. In a separate but parallel tool call, get a third cat image and describe what that cat is feeling on its own."
)
#> I'll retrieve 2 cat images first and then get a third image separately.
#> ◯ [tool call] get_cat_image(n_images = 2L)
#> ● #> <tool result preview not available>
#> ◯ [tool call] get_cat_image(n_images = 1L)
#> ● #> <tool result preview not available>
```

title: feat: Complete dangling tool requests to avoid API errors
description:
Fixes #459 by completing incomplete tool requests with an empty tool result. 

The implementation focuses on _dangling tool requests only_. In other words, when calling `$chat()` or `$stream()` or related async function via `Chat`, we check if the last message is an assistant message with unanswered tool requests and we add a new user turn with the empty tool results before processing the new input.

Here's a simple example with a tool to get a random number:

``` r
pkgload::load_all()
#> ℹ Loading ellmer

random_number_tool <- tool(
  function(n) sample(1:100, n),
  name = "pick_random_number",
  description = "Pick a random number between 1 and 100.",
  arguments = list(
    n = type_number("Number of random numbers to pick.")
  )
)

chat <- chat_openai(model = "gpt-4.1-nano")
# chat <- chat_anthropic(model = "claude-haiku-4-5-20251001")
chat$register_tool(random_number_tool)

chat$chat("Pick a single random number for me.")
#> ◯ [tool call] pick_random_number(n = 1L)
#> ● #> 95
#> I picked the number 95 for you.
```

If we pretend the chat was truncated, i.e. the user interrupted the action before we could send the tool result back to the LLM, the turns would look something like this:

```r
chat$set_turns(chat$get_turns()[1:2]) # Keep user input and tool request
chat$get_turns()
#> [[1]]
#> <Turn: user>
#> Pick a single random number for me.
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> <Turn: assistant>
#> [tool request (call_EdrkWPAmiN5KbaGSghAUpuwo)]: pick_random_number(n = 1L)
```

Currently, trying to pick up the conversation at this point would result in an API error because the tool request wasn't completed. With this PR, however, the chat can be continued normally.

```r
chat$chat("Try again")
#> ◯ [tool call] pick_random_number(n = 1L)
#> ● #> 52
#> The random number I picked for you is 52.
```

Inspecting the chat shows the new user turn with the empty tool request telling the LLM that the chat was interrupted and the tool wasn't invoked.

```r
chat
#> <Chat OpenAI/gpt-4.1-nano turns=7 input=308 output=42 cost=$0.00>
#> ── user ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Pick a single random number for me.
#> ── assistant [input=65 output=15 cost=$0.00] ───────────────────────────────────
#> [tool request (call_EdrkWPAmiN5KbaGSghAUpuwo)]: pick_random_number(n = 1L)
#> ── user ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> [tool result  (call_EdrkWPAmiN5KbaGSghAUpuwo)]: Error: Chat ended before the tool could be invoked.
#> ── user ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Try again
#> ── assistant [input=109 output=15 cost=$0.00] ──────────────────────────────────
#> [tool request (call_9qXCmh4p8QMwLi0TzXaeRrHe)]: pick_random_number(n = 1L)
#> ── user ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> [tool result  (call_9qXCmh4p8QMwLi0TzXaeRrHe)]: 52
#> ── assistant [input=134 output=12 cost=$0.00] ──────────────────────────────────
#> The random number I picked for you is 52.
```

Note that we insert a separate user message primarily because of [the bug discussed in #735](https://github.com/tidyverse/ellmer/pull/735#discussion_r2491983191): inserting tool results into the new user message hits the incorrect behavior described in the linked comment and doesn't work with OpenAI (and a few other providers). I also think conceptually it's better to have this stored as separate user messages, but it also wouldn't be hard to inject to tool results into the new actual user message after #735.

title: Fix on_error='return' behavior in parallel_chat functions
description:
This is a PR to the branch that is currently in #789 - a PR into a PR.

@hadley I tested the `on_error = "return"` behaviour and found it wasn't working as expected - it was returning all results just like `on_error = "continue"`. I used my reprex code from https://github.com/tidyverse/ellmer/issues/628#issuecomment-3096621553 with testing the various `on_error` options. In that test, the fifth input fails because it exceeds the max context window.

The issue is that when requests are executed in parallel with `max_active = 10`, even if request number 5 fails, requests 6-9 still complete successfully. The fix needed was to filter results in `multi_convert()` to keep only results up to and including the first error.

I've pushed a fix to my fork that properly implements the "stop at first error" behavior:
- Commit: https://github.com/kbenoit/ellmer/commit/359a142
- Branch: https://github.com/kbenoit/ellmer/tree/parallel-on-error

The fix adds logic in `multi_convert()` to truncate results at the first error when `on_error = "return"`, and includes tests to verify the behaviour. It seems a bit drastic (and wasteful) to truncate the results but it does provide a behaviour that is now as advertised, which is "return: stop processing and return all responses so far, including any errors."

Changes made:

1. **Modified `multi_convert()` in `R/parallel-chat.R`**:
   - Find the first error in the results
   - Keep only results up to and including that error
   - Discard any results after the first error, even if they succeeded

2. **Added early return logic in `parallel_chat()`**:
   - Stop processing tool calls when `on_error = "return"` and an error occurs

3. **Added comprehensive tests in `test-parallel-chat.R`**:
   - Verify `on_error = "return"` stops at first error
   - Verify `on_error = "continue"` processes all requests
   - All existing tests still pass (48 tests in parallel-chat suite)

I also merged the latest changes from main - these were hung up just after [fe9dff9](https://github.com/tidyverse/ellmer/pull/789/commits/fe9dff99810858fabe3182d98c21d1b3ef39517a) because of merge conflicts, but those were just regarding NEWS.md updates.
